title: Music that spans generations. A story rooted in history. And a rhythm...
transcript: I've always heard that music transcends language, and nothing has ever proved that more to me than the Buena Vista Social Club. I, unfortunately don't speak Spanish, so I was nervous about a show where all of the music is in a language I don't speak. But I didn't need to be, because this is the kind of music that you feel uncontainable joy, aching nostalgia. The music carries decades of love and loss and resilience, and that is very much the story of this musical. Buena Vista Social Club is told through two different timelines. First, in the 1950s on the Eve of the, where a group of young musicians pour their hearts into their music. The next, 40 years later, where a passionate music producer is trying to reunite these artists to record an album of golden era, even music that has almost been lost. The stories are woven together in this really beautiful way, and I love getting to see the characters through multiple generations. The performances are unbelievable and. And the musicians bring so much passion and joy to the stage, which makes it impossible not to get swept up in the emotion and the history. Buena Vista Social Club is more than just a show. It's a Celebration, and you have to go see it.
classificationReason: Creator shares a sustained first-hand opinion of the Broadway production — discusses the music, dual-timeline story structure, performances, and recommends it as 'more than just a show.' Personal nervousness about the Spanish-language music implies attendance.
